items.title: Got a frozen shoulder? It could be due to your blood sugar and genes
items.text: Frozen shoulder can develop seemingly out of nowhere. One day your shoulder feels uncomfortable. A few months later, even putting on a coat or reaching into a cupboard can be difficult. Research on blood sugar offers a clue to why some people are more likely to develop it, particularly those living with diabetes.

items.title: Brainstem atlas reveals possible REM sleep center in humans
items.text: During REM sleep, we dream and our muscles relax into a temporary paralysis called atonia. People with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder—or iRBD—lack atonia, causing them to shout or violently move their arms and legs during REM sleep. This disorder may also be an early symptom of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's or dementia with Lewy bodies, as many people with iRBD later develop these disorders.
